clue.text: Flavours for cocktails and beers

definitions.meaning: aromatic herbal essences such as Angostura, shaken in drops into mixed drinks
in Britain a bitter is a well-hopped draught ale, so several are pints of it

explanation.surface: A list of things a barman keeps behind the counter for mixed drinks and pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one plural word: bar flavourings like Angostura, and pints of the hoppy British ale called bitter.

clue.text: Having two feet like a piebald variety

indicators.note: a different variety of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Standing on two legs, like a variety of pied horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges PIEBALD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipedal creature walks upright on two legs.

clue.text: He has no substance, the chap from Wells

definitions.meaning: a person with no visible body, a figure lacking solid presence
H. G. Wells wrote a novel about a scientist who becomes unseeable

explanation.surface: A man without substance, from the city of Wells in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' looks like the Somerset cathedral city; it is the novelist H. G. Wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Griffin, title character of a famous H. G. Wells novel, cannot be seen.

clue.text: Killing sort of fine for a Norseman

definitions.meaning: in old Irish law a blood-fine paid by a killer to the victim's kin
a Scandinavian man's name, as in the Viking explorer known as the Red

explanation.surface: A Viking pays a fine for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic legal penalty for homicide shares its name with the Viking who discovered Greenland.

clue.text: Warehouse charge undergoes so great a revision

indicators.note: the letters undergo a revision, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A depot's fees go up steeply after a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoes ... a revision' rearranges SO GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage can mean the fee paid for keeping goods in a warehouse.

clue.text: Sole highwayman?

parts.note: the sole is the pad of the foot, so a highwayman who goes on foot rather than horseback is named after it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like 'only', as in the one robber; it is the underside of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a robber who held up travellers while walking, not mounted.

clue.text: Row about engineers' goods in Hull?

indicators.note: the word for a quarrel goes about the engineers

parts.note: a row is a quarrel, a fight
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: An argument among engineers over merchandise in the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the English port city; it is a ship's hull, where cargo is carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo carried in the body of a ship.

clue.text: Circular letter directed to hospital — some swear by it

parts.note: O is the round letter
at means aimed toward
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A round-robin mailed to a hospital that people rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular letter' suggests a mail-out; it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise is something people swear by, invoking a god or holy book.

clue.text: Covered wagon of plain glass

parts.note: a prairie is a large flat grassy plain
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: A canvas-topped wagon crossing grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'grass' is an OCR misread of 'glass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneers crossed the American plains in a canvas-topped wagon nicknamed after a sailing ship.

clue.text: Most senior lady longing to be finished outside

indicators.note: the word for finished goes outside the craving

parts.note: done means finished
a yen is a longing or craving

clue.text: Ambassador of nonpareil type, it turns out

indicators.note: the letters of the three words turn out a different way, rearranged into a single long word

explanation.surface: An envoy described as a matchless sort of person, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges NONPAREIL, TYPE and IT, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat given full powers to act for a government is an envoy of the highest rank.

clue.text: Small depression amid garden trees

indicators.note: the answer lies amid the letters where the two words join

explanation.surface: A little hollow in the ground among the trees of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' points into gar(DEN T)rees.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a slight hollow pressed into a surface.

clue.text: Lighter way to push clumsily

to shove one's way rudely or awkwardly, as through a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone describing a less heavy way of shoving awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' reads as 'less heavy' but is the noun for a cargo boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal or harbour cargo boat, and also a verb for blundering roughly into people.

clue.text: A bit charged right inside golf, club

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the charged particle

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle, a small bit of matter

explanation.surface: Something electrically charged turning up at a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, one of the metal-headed clubs is named for the metal it was made of.

clue.text: Conduct is mainly good in Scotland

indicators.note: the shortened word sits in the Scots word for good

indicators.note: most of the little word is kept, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Behaviour that is mostly good north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims IS to I, which goes in GUDE, Scottish for good, as 'Scotland' marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct someone is to lead or escort them.

clue.text: The moment I get very loud in extremes of jealousy

the first and last letters of the word are used

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A moment when someone shouts angrily in a fit of jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of jealousy' gives J and Y, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiffy is a very short time, an instant.

clue.text: Holiday isle sorted out by river

indicators.note: the letters of the island word are sorted into a new order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A holiday island being organised beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' turns ISLE into LEIS; the Ure is a north-of-England river.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time away from work, as on a holiday, is synonymous with leisure.

clue.text: Roadcraft, we hear, of three big banks

definitions.text: Roadcraft, we hear, of three big banks

parts.words: Roadcraft, we hear, of three big banks
parts.note: said out loud, roadcraft sounds like rowed craft, a vessel propelled by oars; three big banks are three tiers of rowers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roadcraft' suggests driving skill and 'banks' suggests money, but it is a rowed vessel with three tiers of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek warship was driven by oarsmen seated in three tiers on each side.

clue.text: Bone found by archaeological excavation-there'll be a noisy party!

parts.note: the shin is the shinbone, the front of the lower leg
a dig is an archaeological excavation site

explanation.surface: Finding a bone on an excavation is cause for a loud celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is informal slang for a lively, rowdy party or celebration.

clue.text: No mean poet

definitions.meaning: someone who is not stingy or tight-fisted
Stephen ... was an English poet of the 1930s

explanation.surface: A remarkable poet, no ordinary one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No mean poet' reads as praise; it is two senses, a free-handed person and Stephen Spender.
explanation.definitionFit: A big spender is the opposite of a miser, and the name belongs to the English poet Stephen.

clue.text: Greedy sort puts on weight after surfeit of food

indicators.note: the weight unit is placed after the excess

parts.note: a glut is an excess supply
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A greedy person piles on the pounds after overeating.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton is someone who eats and drinks too much.

clue.text: Expert, around here in France, produces loss

indicators.note: the word for skilful goes around the French word

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
ici is French for here

explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall, an amount by which money spent exceeds income.

clue.text: Bunyan's giant depression

definitions.meaning: in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, the giant of Doubting Castle
deep low spirits, loss of hope

explanation.surface: A giant from Bunyan who brings gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Pilgrim's Progress Christian is imprisoned by Giant Despair in Doubting Castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is a state of depression, and also the name of Bunyan's ogre.

clue.text: Changes singlet, feels itching sensation

indicators.note: the word changes, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a vest because it is itchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' rearranges SINGLET; a singlet is a British vest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tingles means experiences a prickling, stinging sensation.

clue.text: Shocking things in Freshwater, say

parts.note: electric fish of rivers and lakes give an electric shock; Freshwater is also a town on the Isle of Wight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' suggests scandal, and the capital F makes Freshwater a place; it means creatures in fresh water that give electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric eels are freshwater fish able to stun prey with a powerful electric discharge.

clue.text: External appearance chaps spoke of

indicators.note: the word is as spoken, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

parts.note: chaps and guys both mean men or fellows

explanation.surface: Men talking about how things look from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or semblance, often one assumed to conceal something.

clue.text: Doctor has a name for this complaint

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor in the forces

explanation.surface: A doctor naming an illness for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as an ailment brought to a doctor; it is a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a grumble or grievance voiced about something.

clue.text: Ruin a French party

parts.note: un is French for a
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A French party being spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to ruin or reverse its effect.

clue.text: Something one can slip in a personal column

definitions.text: Something one can slip in a personal column

parts.words: Something one can slip in a personal column
parts.note: the personal column is one's own spinal column, where a cushion between vertebrae may slip

explanation.walkthrough: 'personal column' suggests newspaper small ads; it is one's backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipped disc is a displaced cushion of cartilage between vertebrae.

clue.text: Me, a London artist-most unorthodox of the show

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are arranged in a highly irregular way to form a new word

explanation.surface: A London painter describing his work as the oddest part of an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most unorthodox' rearranges ME A LONDON ARTIST, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrational describes something relating to a showing or demonstration.

clue.text: Telephoned operator-no change to get capital

in the UK the operator was reached by dialling 0, written as the letter O

explanation.walkthrough: 'change' swaps NO to ON. Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon was formerly the capital city of Burma, now Myanmar.

clue.text: Registers more than one 25

definitions.meaning: official lists or logs that keep written accounts
25 down is a flat round object of music, and several of them are gramophone discs

explanation.surface: Lists of official entries described alongside the plural of a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are the same plural: written logs of events, and vinyl discs for playing music.
